newsitem.title: FRANCE: SOCCER-FRENCH FIRST DIVISION MIDWEEK FIXTURES.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-FRENCH FIRST DIVISION MIDWEEK FIXTURES.

text.p: Matches scheduled for this week in the French first division:

Despite the absence of injured Belgian playmaker Enzo Scifo, Monaco are playing well at the moment, which is bad news for Marseille as the former European champions are going through hard times and urgently need a good result to avoid a deep crisis.

Bastia, still without injured Slovakian midfielder Lubomir Moravcik, will be eager to bounce back after losing 3-0 to Paris St Germain on Sunday. But Lyon want to confirm their recovery after beating Rennes 2-0 on Saturday for the first match under new trainer Bernard Lacombe.
Rennes will welcome the return from suspension of Stephane Guivarc'h, the league top scorer with 12 goals, to face Le Havre, who have been sliding down the standings.

Lowly Nice have every reason to be afraid of leaders PSG, back at their brilliant best as they proved by crushing Bastia 3-0 at Parc des Princes on Sunday. Paris manager Ricardo could be without Brazilian midifielder Leonardo, who has a sore ankle.
Champions Auxerre, currently third, impressed by winning 2-0 at Le Havre on Saturday. They need another win to keep in touch with PSG and Monaco.

One of the highlights of this week's programme, the clash between the two Northern clubs promises to be an exciting one as Lille are doing surprisingly well while Lens are recovering from a series of poor results.
Beaten 3-1 by Monaco on Saturday, Bordeaux will be eager to restore some pride against lowly Cannes and will count on striker Jean-Pierre Papin, unlucky lately and desperately wanting to score.
Strasbourg want to avenge their 3-1 trouncing by Nantes when they face Montpellier, struggling to avoid relegation.
Caen just won 2-1 at bottom-of-the-table Nancy in an all-important match but they might have to fight hard against Nantes, on their way up after a disastrous start to the season.
It already looks all over for newly-promoted Nancy, who have only managed one victory in 15 matches and will probably return to the second division at the end of the season.
